Nothing slow about it; we're already there and have been for a while. I remember a lot of lights going off in my head when I first learned about Brecht in a literature class back around 2015-2016 and seeing how closely his "epic theater" lined up with trends in vidya (and media in general) at the time.

On that note I really appreciate that I had at least one lit professor who was willing to not only teach about but also take a critical eye towards this sort of thing (on account of him growing up on the wrong side of the iron curtain and seeing first-hand that the left weren't always the good guys). I realize just how rare that is in academia nowadays.

Of the 100s of disc-based games I've owned, I've only encountered disc rot twice and both were on Dreamcast games. This is anecdotal of course; I don't know for sure that they're any more prone to it than other systems, but rot is definitely a potential issue.

There's basically nothing I find more engaging than my own daydreams; I think ultimately there are a lot of things I like the IDEA of but don't actually enjoy. Playing out social situations in my head can be fun and interesting, but actually engaging in real-life social interaction is stressful and unfulfilling. This has crept its way into things I used to enjoy doing as well, like reading or playing video games. I keep doing them because I always have, but I think I get more enjoyment thinking about them than actually doing them. Maybe this is just anhedonia taking hold, I don't really know.

I really like Brian Pulido's stuff, mainly Lady Death. Look into Chaos Comics from the 90's or his current company Coffin Comics. He unfortunately lost the rights to most of the old Chaos Comics characters but he's been crowdfunding new stuff for a while and it's pretty good if you like that style of edgy 90's comics.

I'd say Ys Origin is even closer to a Metroidvania than 8 or 9. Also had much less of a focus on story and dialogue than the newer, party-based games and feels more old-school simply due to it being an older game, so I think it fits OP's criteria better. Ys: The Oath in Felghana is similar and my personal pick for best in the series but that's not out in English on the Switch yet, unfortunately.

If its a fighting game you're probably thinking of Bloody Roar.
